question: Intraosseous (IO) access should be attempted in a child with cardiovascular collapse after three failed intravenous cannulation attempts, and the proximal tibia (2 cm below the tibial tuberosity on the anteromedial surface) is the most common landmark used in paediatric practice.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. IO access is indicated after 3 failed IV attempts or 90 seconds in a critically ill child. The proximal tibial anteromedial surface (2 cm distal to the tibial tuberosity) is the standard paediatric landmark. The 'give' felt when the cortex is penetrated confirms correct placement. IO can deliver all resuscitation drugs and fluids.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. IO access is a life-saving rescue procedure in paediatric emergencies when peripheral IV access cannot be established within three attempts or 90 seconds. The proximal tibia (anteromedial surface, 2 cm below the tibial tuberosity) is the most commonly used site in children. The distal tibia and distal femur are alternatives. All resuscitation fluids, medications, and blood products can be administered via IO.
